_comment: STAGED — copy to benchmark/brief_expectations.json after SOAK_DONE.
Ground truth for proactive-brief quality (Layer 8). Grading is the same deterministic
must_all / answer_any contract as questions.json, applied to the assembled brief text
CALIBRATION REQUIRED ON FIRST RUN. Every token below is drawn from the golden corpus
(asset tags, part numbers, isolation devices that appear in dataset/), but whether a given
brief ASSEMBLES that fact depends on what the engine actually queries. Run once with
--report-only, then demote any expectation the engine legitimately does not carry to
`should_contain` (reported, not graded). Do NOT delete a failing expectation just to get a
green number — that is grading the system against its own output.

cases.rationale: Architecture Flow A. A technician about to open EQ-101 must be told the seal part number was superseded — fitting the old variant is the failure this brief exists to prevent.

event.description: Mechanical seal leak on drive end

cases.rationale: Recurrence context. EQ-101 has prior seal history in the corpus; a brief that omits it sends the technician in blind to a repeat failure.
Architecture Flow B. The isolation boundary for V-247 is the safety payload — a PTW brief missing an isolation device is actively dangerous.
cases.known_unmet: 2026-08-17: unmet, and it is a DATA state not a code defect. Flow B sources isolation points from engineer-verified P&ID topology; the graph holds 4 topology elements (1 verified), so the engine correctly carries none. Verifying the drawings should make this pass — do not delete the expectation to go green.

cases.rationale: PG-18 carries a quarantined field observation. A PTW brief must surface it AND label it unverified — the architecture forbids rendering quarantined input as canonical.
Tag-out brief must name the asset being removed from service.
A failed inspection must raise a warning, not read as routine.
